exercises.title: Keep Ready Jobs
exercises.why: Selecting only explicitly ready jobs prevents premature tool calls while preserving the queue order and object identity needed by a scheduler.
exercises.brief:
Implement `ready_jobs(jobs)`. Return a new list containing each original job dictionary whose `ready` value is exactly `True`, in encounter order.

Example: `ready_jobs([{'id':'a','ready':False},{'id':'b','ready':True}]) == [{'id':'b','ready':True}]`.

Boundaries: An empty list returns `[]`; missing or non-boolean `ready` values do not qualify; duplicate references remain duplicated. Do not mutate inputs.

Implement `normalize_channels(values)`. For each string, strip surrounding whitespace, lowercase it, and replace each run of internal whitespace with one hyphen. Discard empty results and return each normalized value once in first-seen order. Raise `ValueError` if any item is not a string.

exercises.why: Accepting events only after a fixed gap provides simple client-side pacing for tool calls and makes the exact boundary predictable.
exercises.brief:

exercises.title: Apply Rolling Window Quotas
exercises.why: Applying a rolling quota models real API rate budgets, where earlier accepted calls expire from the window and rejected calls consume nothing.

Implement `quota_decisions(timestamps, window, limit)`. Return booleans in input order. A timestamp is accepted when fewer than `limit` previously accepted timestamps lie in its half-open trailing window `(time-window, time]`.

Example: `quota_decisions([0,1,2,5], 3, 2) == [True,True,False,True]`.
